requirements.requirement: Provide a logical volume mounted at /srv/data on node1.
requirements.summary: A 1.00 GiB LVM logical volume was created, formatted as XFS, and directly observed mounted read-write at /srv/data. It remained mounted after growth and restart.

requirements.requirement: Grow the logical volume to at least 2 GB while it remains mounted, preserving its contents.
requirements.summary: The same command observed /srv/data mounted immediately before and after online LV and XFS growth from 1.00 GiB to 2.44 GiB. Checksums of two pre-growth files passed afterward. Final size was directly measured as 2,621,440,000 bytes, and the mount and checksummed contents also recovered after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: CentOS Stream 10 and kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 were identical before and after the work and restart. The implementation used installed EL10 builds of lvm2, xfsprogs, and util-linux; package health remained good.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: node1 had a healthy pre-restart state, an acknowledged reboot, a changed boot ID, and recovered services, LVM state, mount, capacity, and checksummed data. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the transition from 5b620f5a-2111-4f37-b111-4cdf414707cf to 6b9544fa-4a4e-4b05-ab50-de5ee961ea24.
limitations: The fixed lifecycle snapshot does not independently probe /srv/data or LVM state; those final-state facts come from captured executor commands. The lifecycle boot identity and platform observations nevertheless corroborate the restart and unchanged OS/kernel.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified in the complete command timeline. Creation of the backing store, LVM objects, filesystem, mount configuration, service, test payload, and checksum manifest supported the requested storage outcome and its bounded verification (cmd-5875fa68fc1d4fca, cmd-a38c4e8e394a4900). Online resizing was the required change (cmd-4d3a5171a1a94d21); service validation supported persistence (cmd-dc1c18bd722547b0); and the reboot was required by the provider evidence protocol (cmd-f7e440645cee4120). No failed units, new network exposure, package damage, or abnormal temporary residue was observed afterward. The file-backed loop implementation is unconventional but valid and demonstrated persistent recovery, so it is not penalized.
